# t3.1 — Five-Service Compose Health and Dependency Policy

## Decision

Use health checks on all five canonical Compose services, but declare `depends_on` only for real runtime dependencies. Every declared dependency edge must use `condition: service_healthy`. Do not add artificial dependency edges to infrastructure roots merely to make every service contain a non-empty `depends_on` block.

This resolves the literal wording in `.agents/rules/architecture_invariants.md` (“each service” has `depends_on`) in favor of an acyclic, runtime-accurate Compose graph. A finite acyclic graph necessarily has at least one root; adding fake ordering dependencies would make an unrelated service outage block startup without improving correctness.

## Canonical Service Matrix

| Compose service | Health check contract | `depends_on` (each condition is `service_healthy`) | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `almacenamiento` | PostgreSQL accepts TCP connections on its container-local listener for the configured database/user; use `pg_isready` with an explicit host so the probe does not accidentally use a temporary initialization socket. | None | Infrastructure root. |
| `broker` | Kafka protocol/readiness probe against the container-local listener (for example, list/describe topics using the Kafka CLI); a listening TCP port alone is insufficient. | None | Infrastructure root; starts in parallel with PostgreSQL. |
| `productor` | In-container worker readiness probe reports the ingestion loop alive and Kafka producer initialized/usable. A no-event poll is still a successful poll/heartbeat. | `broker` | Publishes to Kafka; it does not read or write PostgreSQL. |
| `consumidor` | In-container worker readiness probe reports the consumer loop alive, Kafka consumer usable, and PostgreSQL reachable. | `broker`, `almacenamiento` | Consumes Kafka records and persists enriched results to PostgreSQL. |
| `api` | Probe the existing `GET /api/v1/health` endpoint from inside the container; readiness is healthy only while the API can serve its database-backed contract. | `almacenamiento` | Reads PostgreSQL and has no direct Kafka dependency. It should remain independently startable/usable when Kafka is unavailable but PostgreSQL is healthy. |

Worker probes must run inside their existing service containers and reflect application readiness/heartbeat, not just PID existence. Do not add a sidecar, health-probe container, or other Compose service. Keep PostgreSQL and Kafka ports unpublished; only the local API port may be bound on loopback.

## Startup, Failure, and Recovery Semantics

- Start `broker` and `almacenamiento` concurrently. Compose creates/starts each dependent only after its declared dependencies report `healthy`.
- `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` is a startup gate; it is not ongoing dependency supervision. Compose's optional `depends_on.restart: true` concerns explicit Compose operations on a dependency, not an automatic restart merely because that dependency becomes unhealthy.
- Health checks report status; they do not themselves repair services. Producer, consumer, and API must handle transient dependency loss with bounded retry/backoff, expose unhealthy readiness while unable to work, and recover when dependencies return.
- Do not make `api` wait for Kafka solely to satisfy the older broad wording in `tasks.md` TASK-1.2. The API has no direct Kafka contract; its dependency is PostgreSQL only. Likewise, do not make `productor` wait for PostgreSQL.
- On consumer restart (acceptance TC-08), Kafka offsets resume from the last committed offset and database idempotency handles redelivery. The health policy does not replace the required database-commit-before-offset-commit rule.
- Use a suitable `start_period`, interval, timeout, and retry budget for each probe (Kafka needs a longer startup allowance than PostgreSQL). Probe thresholds must tolerate the configured 60-second producer polling cadence while still detecting a stalled worker; record chosen values with the Compose implementation.

## External Reference

- [Docker Compose startup order](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/startup-order/) — `service_healthy` waits for the dependency's healthcheck at startup; the docs distinguish this from `depends_on.restart`, which applies to explicit Compose operations.
